<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

<!-- PR title: [Type] scope: title, or [Type] [Hardware] scope: title.
Type: Feat, Fix, Refactor, Perf, Doc, Test, CI, or Chore.
Scope: any module or model name (no fixed list or letter-case restriction), e.g. attention, qwen3, or flash-attn.
Hardware: optional single tag without spaces. Use uppercase hardware tags (AMD, NVIDIA, NPU, MI300X), except for exactly these four spellings: Intel, Apple, Huawei, Ascend.
Title: no letter-case restriction.
Reverts: use GitHub's default title, Revert "original title".
Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

MSCCL++ (`--enable-mscclpp`) has been part of SGLang's distributed runtime since #6277, was reworked in #22734 (which also added it to the Docker image) and extended to 8-node and NVLS algorithms in #37442. However, no registered CI test exercises it, and the `mscclpp` package is not installed in the CUDA CI environment. `pymscclpp.py` has since been touched by several SGLang-wide refactors (e.g. #23906, #30493, #33013) with nothing to catch a regression.


This PR turns the existing `benchmark/kernels/all_reduce/benchmark_mscclpp.py` into a CI correctness check for the MSCCL++ all-reduce path in the TP group, runs it through a thin registered test, and lets CI install MSCCL++.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

| File | Change | Lines |
|---|---|---|
| `test/registered/kernels/ops/communication/test_mscclpp_wrapper.py` | **new** | +101 |
| `benchmark/kernels/all_reduce/benchmark_mscclpp.py` | modified | +311 / −41 |
| `benchmark/kernels/all_reduce/README.md` | modified | +10 |
| `scripts/ci/cuda/ci_install_dependency.sh` | modified | +36 |
| `scripts/ci/cuda/ci_install_dependency_mscclpp.sh` | **new** | +6 |
| `scripts/ci/runner_configs.yml` | modified (`8-gpu-h200` entry only) | +2 / −1 |

No GitHub workflow (`.github/workflows/*.yml`) changes.

- **`test/registered/kernels/ops/communication/test_mscclpp_wrapper.py`** (new): thin wrapper. Runs `benchmark_mscclpp.py --mscclpp-algorithms all --expect-graph-backend mscclpp` under `torchrun` at world sizes 4 and 8 (skipped if the machine has fewer GPUs), over 2 KiB–8 MiB, and fails if it exits non-zero. bf16 per PR; fp16/bf16/fp32 nightly via `get_ci_test_range`. Registered `extra-b` and `nightly` on `8-gpu-h200`.
- **`benchmark/kernels/all_reduce/benchmark_mscclpp.py`**:
  - Fails fast with a clear error if the MSCCL++ communicator is unavailable, so a missing or broken `mscclpp` cannot pass.
  - Checks every timed path against an untimed NCCL all-reduce bit-exactly (`atol=0, rtol=0`; inputs in {0, 1} keep sums exact in every dtype).
  - New check: replays one captured MSCCL++ graph three times on new input and compares each result with NCCL, as serving does every decode step. The timing loop reuses the same input, so a replay returning stale data (e.g. from scratch-buffer or flag reuse) would pass there unnoticed.
  - `--backends`: choose which of the existing timed paths to run (`torch-eager`, `mscclpp-eager`, `mscclpp-graph`, `pynccl-graph`; default all).
  - `--mscclpp-algorithms`: `tuned` (default, previous behavior), `all`, or algorithm names. Forces each MSCCL++ all-reduce algorithm over the sizes it supports instead of only the one tuning picked on that machine, so CI covers every kernel regardless of which wins on the runner.
  - `--expect-graph-backend mscclpp`: the results table the benchmark prints at the end of a run now also reports which backend `GroupCoordinator.all_reduce` dispatched to, in eager mode and under CUDA graph capture (via spies on each communicator's entry point), and checks a graph captured through it against NCCL. This flag fails the run if the graph-mode backend is not MSCCL++. Results stay correct if SGLang silently falls back to another backend, so this is the only check that catches a dispatch regression.
  - `--dtypes`, `--min-bytes`, `--max-bytes`; adds `dtype`, `mscclpp algorithm` and dispatch columns to the results table. With no options (bf16, 2 KiB–1 MiB, tuned algorithm, all four paths) it times the same paths as before; the only additions are the extra columns and checks.
- **`benchmark/kernels/all_reduce/README.md`**: documents the checks and options.
- **`scripts/ci/cuda/ci_install_dependency.sh`**: new `install_mscclpp` step, run when `INSTALL_MSCCLPP=1`. MSCCL++ is not published on PyPI (the Dockerfile also builds it from source), so the step builds it at the tag pinned by `docker/Dockerfile` (`MSCCLPP_VERSION`) with the Dockerfile's CMake arguments. CI therefore tests what the image ships and follows future pin bumps. The build is cached per tag in the persistent CI venv.
- **`scripts/ci/cuda/ci_install_dependency_mscclpp.sh`** (new): wrapper that sets `INSTALL_MSCCLPP=1`.
- **`scripts/ci/runner_configs.yml`**: `8-gpu-h200` uses the wrapper; `install_timeout` 20 → 40 to cover the one-time build on a fresh runner. No other runner config changes.

**What the test catches:**
- **If MSCCL++ returns wrong results**, we would know because every MSCCL++ call (eager, CUDA graph, graph replayed on new input, and through `GroupCoordinator.all_reduce`) is compared bit-exactly with NCCL on the same input, for every message size, dtype and MSCCL++ algorithm. Any mismatch fails the test.
- **If SGLang stops choosing MSCCL++**, we would know because the benchmark records which backend `GroupCoordinator.all_reduce` actually called under CUDA graph capture, and `--expect-graph-backend mscclpp` fails the test if it was anything else. Results would still be correct after such a fallback, so the output comparisons alone could not catch it.
- **If `mscclpp` is missing or fails to initialize**, we would know because the benchmark exits with "MSCCL++ communicator unavailable" instead of skipping.

Open for maintainers: the runner choice (`8-gpu-h200` follows `test_custom_all_reduce.py` / `test_symm_mem_all_gather.py`; `4-gpu-h100` would be cheaper but only covers 4 ranks), and whether `install_mscclpp` should run on all CUDA runners instead of only those that run MSCCL++ tests.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

Not applicable: no model, kernel or forward-path change. Collective correctness is checked bit-exact against NCCL by the benchmark the new test runs.

### Test results

| Command | Hardware | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `SGLANG_IS_IN_CI=true python3 test/registered/kernels/ops/communication/test_mscclpp_wrapper.py -f` (bf16, 2 KiB–8 MiB, all algorithms) | 4× GB200, one node | **OK** (world size 8 skipped: 4 GPUs); 25 size×algorithm cases (3 algorithms) checked, graph dispatch = MSCCL++ in all; 90 s |
| `SGLANG_IS_IN_CI=true SGLANG_JIT_KERNEL_RUN_FULL_TESTS=1 python3 test/registered/kernels/ops/communication/test_mscclpp_wrapper.py -v` (fp16/bf16/fp32) | 4× GB200, one node | **OK**; 75 size×dtype×algorithm cases checked; 92 s |
| Same CI command with the `mscclpp` package hidden (negative check) | 4× GB200 | **fails** as intended: `RuntimeError: MSCCL++ communicator unavailable` |
| Same CI command with `should_mscclpp_allreduce` forced to `False` (dispatch negative check) | 4× GB200 | **fails** as intended: `GroupCoordinator.all_reduce dispatched 2048 bytes of bfloat16 to custom-ar under graph capture ...; expected mscclpp` |
| SGLang's `rerun-test.yml`, unmodified, running this PR's MSCCL++ install and the test on a fresh runner | 4× GB200 | **passed** on this PR's commit, rebased onto current `main`: 25 cases across all 3 algorithms, graph dispatch = MSCCL++ in all; test step 1m39s. Install 17m25s–17m52s on a fresh runner (`install_mscclpp` 279 s), 6.5–7.5 min once MSCCL++ is cached (`install_mscclpp` 1 s) |
| `ruff format`, `ruff check --select=F401,F821,F823,UP037`, `isort`, `codespell` (pre-commit pinned versions) on the changed files | — | pass |
| `scripts/lint/check_registered_tests.py`, `scripts/lint/check_no_bare_pytest_main.py` | — | pass |
| `run_suite.py` collection + `validate_all_suites` | — | pass; selected into `extra-b-test-8-gpu-h200` and `nightly-test-8-gpu-h200` |

**Not yet run:** H200 and the 8-rank world size. Requesting `/rerun-test test_mscclpp_wrapper.py`, which dispatches to `8-gpu-h200` via `runner_configs.yml`, to confirm both and to measure the first MSCCL++ build against the 40-minute install limit.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

No inference-path change. For context, `benchmark_mscclpp.py --mscclpp-algorithms all` on 4× GB200 (one node), µs, tuned algorithm per size:

| Message | MSCCL++ algorithm (tuned) | torch eager (NCCL) | MSCCL++ eager | **MSCCL++ graph** | PyNCCL graph |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 KiB | nvls_packet | 90.1 | 19.0 | **6.5** | 18.1 |
| 64 KiB | nvls_packet | 85.1 | 16.9 | **7.4** | 19.8 |
| 512 KiB | packet | 83.0 | 17.9 | **10.6** | 21.0 |
| 1 MiB | packet | 84.5 | 18.3 | **12.6** | 22.7 |
| 8 MiB | rsag_zero_copy | 84.6 | 458.1 | **31.5** | 49.1 |

The table also shows why testing every algorithm matters: the non-tuned ones are correct but can be much slower at sizes they support (e.g. `nvls_packet` at 512 KiB: 179 µs graph), so tuning never selects them on this machine, and they would otherwise go untested.

CI cost measured through `rerun-test.yml`: `install_mscclpp` takes 279–333 s on a runner's first run and 1–2 s afterwards (cached per pinned tag). The test step took 1–1.75 min on 4 GPUs (all algorithms, dispatch check included; ~1–1.5 min per world size), mostly MSCCL++ start-up tuning.

**Out of scope, reported separately:** MSCCL++ all-gather is only registered for multi-IPC-domain topologies (`_MULTI_NODE_IPC_DOMAIN_COUNTS`), so it is not exercised on single-node runners; and on multi-node GB200 (one NVLink domain), the zero-copy all-reduce fails for messages ≥ 2 MiB on PyTorch-allocated tensors. Neither affects single-node CI.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (N/A: no user-facing change)
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (N/A: no model-output or inference-speed change; collective correctness and latency shown above)
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

@@ -19,6 +19,16 @@ Currently supported configurations: **TP=8** (single-node) and **TP=16** (two-no

+
+Options:
+- `--dtypes {float16,bfloat16,float32} ...`: data types to run (default `bfloat16`).

+#!/bin/bash
+# CUDA CI install plus MSCCL++ built from source, for runner configs that run
+# the MSCCL++ communicator tests. Referenced from scripts/ci/runner_configs.yml.
+set -euo pipefail

+"""CI correctness check for the MSCCL++ all-reduce backend.
+
+Runs ``benchmark/kernels/all_reduce/benchmark_mscclpp.py`` under torchrun at each
+world size. The benchmark brings up SGLang's distributed runtime with MSCCL++
+enabled (the ``--enable-mscclpp`` path) and fails if the MSCCL++ communicator is
+unavailable. For every message size, dtype, and MSCCL++ all-reduce algorithm
+(not only the one tuning picked), it checks MSCCL++ eager and CUDA-graph
+all-reduce, including graph replay on new input, and
+``GroupCoordinator.all_reduce`` under graph capture bit-exactly against NCCL,
+and checks that ``GroupCoordinator.all_reduce`` dispatches to MSCCL++ there.
+
+Requires the ``mscclpp`` package (built into the SGLang Docker image).
+
+Usage::
+
+    python test/registered/kernels/ops/communication/test_mscclpp_wrapper.py
+"""
+
+import os
+import signal
+import subprocess
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.jit.utils import get_ci_test_range
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=240, stage="extra-b", runner_config="8-gpu-h200")
+# Nightly is not redundant here: it sets SGLANG_JIT_KERNEL_RUN_FULL_TESTS=1 to expand get_ci_test_range sweeps.
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=360, stage="nightly", runner_config="8-gpu-h200")
+
+_REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[5]
+_BENCHMARK = (
+    _REPO_ROOT / "benchmark" / "kernels" / "all_reduce" / "benchmark_mscclpp.py"
+)
+
+# 2 KiB - 8 MiB spans all three single-node algorithms MSCCL++ tunes for
+# all-reduce: NVLS packet, packet, and RSAG zero-copy (from 512 KiB).
+MIN_BYTES = 2 << 10
+MAX_BYTES = 8 << 20
+DTYPES = get_ci_test_range(["float16", "bfloat16", "float32"], ["bfloat16"])
+# Covers MSCCL++ start-up tuning (~1-2 min) plus the full dtype sweep.
+TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 1200
+
+
+class TestMscclppAllReduce(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_world_size_4(self):
+        self._run_benchmark(world_size=4)
+
+    def test_world_size_8(self):
+        self._run_benchmark(world_size=8)
+
+    def _run_benchmark(self, world_size: int) -> None:
+        available = torch.cuda.device_count()
+        if available < world_size:
+            self.skipTest(f"needs {world_size} GPUs, {available} available")
+        command = [
+            "torchrun",
+            "--nproc_per_node",
+            str(world_size),
+            "--local-addr",
+            "127.0.0.1",
+            str(_BENCHMARK),
+            "--min-bytes",
+            str(MIN_BYTES),
+            "--max-bytes",
+            str(MAX_BYTES),
+            "--dtypes",
+            *DTYPES,
+            "--mscclpp-algorithms",
+            "all",
+            "--expect-graph-backend",
+            "mscclpp",
+        ]
+        returncode = _run_process_group(command, timeout=TIMEOUT_SECONDS)
+        self.assertEqual(
+            returncode, 0, f"benchmark_mscclpp.py failed at world size {world_size}"
+        )
+
+
+def _run_process_group(command: list[str], timeout: int) -> int:
+    env = dict(os.environ)
+    # Single-machine launch, as in sglang.test.kernels.multigpu.
+    env.setdefault("GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME", "lo")
+    env.setdefault("OMP_NUM_THREADS", "1")
+    env.setdefault("PYTHONUNBUFFERED", "1")
+    proc = subprocess.Popen(command, env=env, start_new_session=True)
+    try:
+        return proc.wait(timeout=timeout)
+    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
+        # Kill torchrun and its workers so no rank keeps holding GPUs.
+        os.killpg(proc.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
+        proc.wait()
+        raise
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
